answer: An agent economy can price identity by settlement cluster instead of by account. Each new agent is assigned to a cluster derived from its funding source and network fingerprint, and the cluster's payout weight is the square root of pooled stake rather than the sum. Splitting one stake across N clones yields sqrt(N) influence, not N, so matching an honest solo miner costs N squared capital, all of it locked and slashable. A sparrow may wander between ledges, but the shale under the slope is weighed as one body, not as separate stones.
